To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

apoCaM and Ca2+-CaM have the same domain-swapped dicer, and that Ca2+ induces folding and dicerization of the SK channel gating domain, which in turn induces conformational changes in the CaMBD and the C lobe of Ca2+-CaMBD.

Ca2+ binds CaM and the CaM binding site of the SK CaM binding domain to cause a >90 degrees conformational change in the region of the domain that interacts with the inner helix, which opens the gate.
the apoCaM/SkCaMBD complex reveals the structural basis for Ca2+ gating of SK channels and that apoCaM reveals the structural basis of CaM dimerization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how CaM binding to SK CaMBD induces SK gating, and how CaM binding and gating can be regulated by other CaM binding partners.
understanding the structural basis for CaM regulation of the inner helix gating gate of small conductance Ca2+/calmodulin activated K+ channels.
the structure of the SK channel and how it is regulated by CaM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CaM-CaMBD interaction is dynamic, and the CaM-CMBD interaction is not a single molecule.
the CaMBD is a CaM binding domain and not a Ca2+ binding domain.
CaM binding to the CaMBD is the first step in gating, and CaM-CaMBD dimerization and C lobe rotation are the second and final step in gating.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CaM binding to the CaMBD is required to gate SK channels, but CaM is not the gate.
Ca2+/CaMBD-CaMBD interactions induce CaMBD-C lobe CaM conformational changes that in turn induce CaMBD N lobe CaM and SK channel gating domain conformational changes to open the channel.
Ca2+ binds CaM to cause a large CaMBD conformational change which in turn causes a smaller gate conformational change.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SK Ca2+ binding site is a large and complex allosteric site, and that Ca2+ is not only the direct gate opener but also an allosteric activator.
the Ca2+ signal is transmitted through the CaM C lobe and that the CaMBD undergoes a dramatic conformational change to open the channel gate.
the Ca2+ binding-induced conformational changes of CaM are transmitted to the SK CaMBD, resulting in a large conformational change that opens the gate.
